rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This RNA-only singleprofile model with PCA encoding tests the simplest configuration to measure baseline performance. Testing this configuration clarifies whether RNA-only models can achieve reasonable accuracy, providing critical evidence for future comparisons with multimodal approaches.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with PCA achieves 0.4849 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (same RNA encoder, no image data), isolating the effect of profile aggregation. It balances exploration of profile settings and aggregation methods while maintaining consistency with the base RNA encoder, providing critical insights into whether multiprofile structure improves performance.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile (config_001). This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation improves performance compared to avgpool in multiprofile RNA-only models. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, a key design choice with potential for significant performance gains.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002: 0.5906 accuracy) outperform singleprofile variants. This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 RNA encoder in the high-performing multiprofile setup with avgpool aggregation. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice while maintaining the proven multiprofile and aggregation strategy, balancing exploitation of current strengths with exploration of encoder alternatives.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.650). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (config_006) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method while keeping RNA encoder and profile setting constant. This balances exploitation of the current best configuration with exploration of a key design choice.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6529). This experiment tests whether combining RNA and image data (multimodal) using the same scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (proven effective in image-only models) can further improve accuracy. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion while leveraging established components, balancing exploration of multimodal benefits with exploitation of prior successes.

The existing evidence shows that rna_only models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.652970). This experiment tests whether using a singleprofile setup with scvi_n200 RNA encoder (no image or aggregation) could yield better results, clarifying the impact of profile setting and aggregation on performance. It balances exploration of profile settings while building on the strong foundation of scvi_n200.

Existing evidence shows rna_only models with scvi_n200 encoder (config_005/006) achieve high accuracy (0.65+). This experiment tests scgpt encoder (a new RNA encoder) in the multiprofile setup with avgpool aggregation, which is the configuration with the highest current accuracy. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice while maintaining the proven multiprofile/avgpool combination, balancing exploration of a new encoder with exploitation of a high-performing setup.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only models with scvi_n200 and multiprofile settings (config_006: 0.652970 accuracy) are strong. This experiment tests multimodal fusion with scvi_n200 (best RNA encoder), imagenet_vit_l (high-performing image encoder), avgpool (effective in RNA-only), and weighted fusion (untested in this context). It clarifies if combining these elements can surpass the current RNA-only best, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of multimodal potential.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_037) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.706). This experiment tests replacing scvi_n200 with scgpt (a more complex RNA encoder) and using transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) to isolate the impact of these changes. It addresses uncertainty about whether scgpt's performance and transformer aggregation could further improve accuracy, leveraging the last budget slot to explore a high-potential combination.
